To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cAMP content of the mouse brain stem is increased following exposure of the animal to 1,1,1-trichlorothane, and that the increased c AMP content may be mediated by adrenergic interaction with the guanidine nucleotide-binding regulatory unit of adenylate cyclas.

inhalation or intraperitonal administration of TCE increased the cAMP level, the activity of the norepinephrin-activated AC and the cAMP content of the brain stem, but had no effect in the cerebellium or hippocampus.
TCE increased the cAMP level and the norepinephine-stimulated adenylate cyclate activity, but not the basal and guanine nucleotide-stimulated adenyalate cyclate activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the action of 1, 1, 2, 2-tetrachloroethane, which is an important industrial solvent and a major component of many commercial products.
the effects of the inhalation or intraperitonial administration of 1,1,1-trichlor-ethane (TCA) on the cAMP-metabolism in the brain of male mice (ICR-strain).
the effects of 1, 1, 2-trichloroethylene (TCE) on the central nervous system (CNS).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TCE has no effect on cAMP metabolism in the brain stem, but that the increase in cAMP content may be a secondary phenomenon.
the effects of TCE are mediated by an increase of cAMP in the brain stem.
1,1-tri-chloroethane is a neurotoxicant, which is capable of altering the cAMP metabolism and thereby the function of the central nervous system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TCE has a stimulatory effect on the c-AMP metabolism in the brain stem.

the increased cAMp level in brain stem induced by 1,1-1-trichlorothane may be mediated via an interaction of adrenoceptors with the guanine-nucleotide binding regulatory component of adenylate cyclases resulting in an increase of the cAMP level.
TCE increases cAMP content in brainstem and this effect may be mediated via activation of the adenylatc cyclase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a novel approach to study the effects of TCE on the cAMP system in the mouse brain.
the use of the cAMP content is not a good indicator of the cAMP level.
TCE can affect the cAMP metabolism of the mouse brain and that the brain stem is the most sensitive brain region.
